subject: Model inventory, provenance & version control — RFP follow-up
messages:
From: Alicia Park <security@acme-corp.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Holt <procurement@acme-corp.com>, security-team@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: model inventory, licensing & provenance details

Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of Acme's RFP security questionnaire we need the following details about Redwoods' served models (hosted API + private deployments):

- A downloadable inventory listing every model you expose to customers (model name, published version(s), weight/weight-source URL, explicit license for weights and code).
- Provenance statement for each model: training org, training datestamp, any 3rd-party checkpoints used.
- For open-models (e.g., Apache/MIT/CC), confirm whether Redwood redistributes weights or only provides API access.
- How you handle downstream derivative/fine-tuned models (who owns the artifact; do you retain or purge?).
- Version pinning & update policy: how customers pin versions, whether auto-updates are enabled by default, and notification workflow for breaking updates.
- Cryptographic checksums (SHA256) or SBOM-style manifests for models and significant artifacts.

We'd prefer a single CSV + short summary narrative we can attach to our security review. Can you get this by EOD Thursday? If not, a short interim note is fine.

Appreciate it,
Alicia
Alicia Park
Head of Security — Acme Corp
[security@acme-corp.com]
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Park <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: model inventory, licensing & provenance details

Alicia —

Thanks for the clear list. We're on it. I'm routing this to our product and legal SMEs (cc'd). We'll assemble a CSV inventory and an annotated summary addressing each bullet. We'll drop a preliminary bundle by end of day Thursday (2026-08-27) and follow up with a formal response plus the checksums and manifests.

Two quick notes up front so expectations align:
- For many open-source models we provide API access from hosted infrastructure; redistribution of raw weights depends on the model's license and on whether the weights are upstream-published (we can confirm per-model).
- For customer-specific fine-tuned artifacts, customers control retention for Private deployments; for Redwood-hosted fine-tuning we have standard retention windows and can provide more restrictive policies under enterprise contracts.

We'll include the pinning/config examples (Console + API) and a sample webhook for update notifications.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0184

[Attachment: RFP_outline_notes.txt (text/plain)]
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Park <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood: model inventory + provenance summary (initial)

Alicia —

Attached are the files: redwood_model_inventory.csv and model_license_matrix.xlsx. Below is a short annotated summary for the key models referenced in your RFP. The CSV includes columns: model_id, public_name, version, weight_source, weight_license, code_license, provenance_summary, sha256_checksum, redistributable (yes/no), redwood_distributes_weights (yes/no).

Summary (high level):
- rw-open-1.0  | version: 2026-05-11 | weight_source: https://hf.co/rw/rw-open-1.0/weights | weight_license: Apache-2.0 (weights) | code_license: MIT | provenance: trained by Redwood Research on mixture of public web + licensed corpora; checkpoint initialized from upstream rw-base-0.8; documented training datestamp and training run-id in CSV | sha256: <provided> | redistributable: yes (per Apache) | redwood_distributes_weights: yes (for enterprise/private customers under distro terms)

- lw-llama2-13b-compat | version: 2026-04-02 | weight_source: upstream_llama2_vendor | weight_license: Llama-2-custom-license (no redistribution) | code_license: MIT | provenance: upstream Meta checkpoint + Redwood fine-tuning; weights not redistributed by Redwood; we provide API access and private-hosting mapping for customers who hold their own redistribution rights | sha256: <provided> | redistributable: no | redwood_distributes_weights: no

- gptx-compat-mini | version: 2025-11-12 | weight_source: licensed third-party provider | weight_license: Commercial license (restricted) | code_license: Apache-2.0 | provenance: licensed third-party weights; Redwood acts as a steward and provides inference access only | redistributable: no

- customer-finetunes/* | versions: customer-specific | weight_source: n/a (customer artifact) | weight_license: customer owned (by default) | provenance: created during customer job; we can export manifests on request | redistributable: only with explicit customer permission

Version pinning + update policy (short):
- Pinning: Customers can pin model by name + explicit version tag in the Console or via API (e.g., model=rw-open-1.0@2026-05-11). Pinning is supported for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Auto-updates: By default we do not auto-upgrade pinned models. For unpinned "floating" model aliases (e.g., rw-open-1.0 -> latest), the Console displays pending updates and customers can opt-in to automatic patch updates. Enterprise customers may elect auto-apply policies with canary rollout controls.
- Notifications: We support email + webhook notifications for model updates, deprecations, and security advisories. We also publish a changelog page per model and provide an RSS/atom feed and HubSpot webhook integration.

Checksums & manifests: CSV contains SHA256 checksums for published weights and a pointer to a machine-readable manifest (SBOM style) for each model. For third-party-licensed weights where redistribution is restricted, we still publish manifest metadata but not raw weight blobs.

Redistribution policy (short):
- Where license permits (Apache-2.0, MIT), Redwood can provide weights for Private/on-prem deployments and (by default) for enterprise redistribution under standard distro terms.
- For vendor-licensed or restricted models (e.g., Meta Llama-2 variants), Redwood provides inference and private-hosting options but does not redistribute weights unless the customer has separate rights.

Attachments included: redwood_model_inventory.csv, model_license_matrix.xlsx, redwood_sla_snapshot.pdf

Next steps: happy to walk through the inventory in a short call and flag any rows you want expanded (training logs, hyperparameters, or run-level manifests).

Cheers,
Vanessa

[Attachment: model_license_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
[Attachment: redwood_sla_snapshot.pdf (application/pdf)]
From: Alicia Park <security@acme-corp.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Holt <procurement@acme-corp.com>, security-team@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood: model inventory + provenance summary (initial)

Vanessa —

This is a great start; thank you. A couple of follow-ups after scanning the CSV:

1) For the Apache-2.0 models you list as redistributable: can you confirm whether the exact weight files you publish include any additional license exceptions or bundled 3rd-party artifacts that would change permissivity? We need an explicit statement that the weight tarballs are clean of non-Apache encumbrances.

2) For upstream vendor checkpoints (e.g., lw-llama2-13b-compat), clarify the mechanism you use to verify the upstream checksum; do you host the checksum on your public manifest or rely on the vendor?

3) For customer fine-tunes hosted on Redwood: what is the default retention period for retained artifacts, and can customers request immediate deletion plus certification?

4) Do you publish per-model notice of data sources used for pretraining (high-level categories are fine: web crawl, licensed crawls, curated corpora)? Acme's data policy requires traceability for models we plan to expose to our customers.

Also: can you provide the SHA256 string for rw-open-1.0 weights and a short canonical provenance snippet suitable for our SOC review?

If it's easier, we can do a 30-min call Thursday morning.

Best,
Alicia
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Park <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood: model inventory + provenance summary (initial)

Alicia —

Looping in legal & product language to make these items explicit. Short answers first, followed by formal phrasing you can reuse in your security pack.

1) Weight tarballs: For models we list as redistributable (Apache/MIT), the published weight files do not contain additional 3rd-party binaries or proprietary bundles. We run an automated scan during packaging; results are available on request. Formal statement: "Redwood certifies that, to the best of its knowledge, redistributable weight artifacts for models listed as Apache-2.0/MIT are packaged without additional proprietary third-party binaries or encumbrances; manifest and scan reports can be provided under NDA as needed."

2) Checksum verification: For upstream checkpoints we compute SHA256 at ingest time, publish the checksum in our model manifest, and retain the original vendor-provided checksum when available. Our public manifest page and the attached CSV include both values and a note when they differ. For internal audit we record run-id, ingest timestamp, and source URL.

3) Fine-tune retention: Default retention for Redwood-hosted fine-tunes is 90 days after job completion; customers may request immediate deletion and attest to deletion via a signed audit if required. For Private/on-prem deployments customers manage retention per their environment.

4) Training data categories: We publish high-level categories in the manifest (web_crawl, licensed_corpora, curated_ebooks, open_datasets). For models trained on licensed or partner datasets we flag the dataset and provide the dataset owner contact where permitted.

Canonical provenance snippet (suitable for your SOC pack):
"rw-open-1.0 — Trained by Redwood Research on 2026-02-15 to 2026-04-30. Training data: web_crawl (filtered), licensed_corpora (provider list available under NDA), curated_public_datasets. Checkpoint initialized from rw-base-0.8. We computed SHA256: abc123def456... (full checksum in attached manifest). Packaging verified free of third-party proprietary binaries as of 2026-05-11."

I'll attach a short legal-approved text file with these statements; happy to expand into a one-page attestation if Acme needs it for auditors.

—Marissa 
Director, Enterprise Contracts, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: license_exceptions.txt (text/plain)]
